display: Ceramicist in Coyoacán, Mexico City, making hand-painted, lead-free talavera-inspired tableware.

signals.text: I'm getting ready for the Day of the Dead market in Coyoacán on 28 October and I'm making a large autumn tableware collection.
A client wants me to recreate her grandmother's plate, which had a little yellow flower. I've finished the sketches and a test tile.
My electric kiln overshoots its target temperature by about 40 degrees and I can't trust it yet. Two firings have been ruined this month.
I can't tell whether the fault is the controller, the relay or the elements. I'm replacing the relay on 4 October and doing a 20-piece test firing on 11 October.
Only 12 of my 40 dinner sets are finished. The other 28 are waiting to be fired and I won't rush them.
I'd like a reliable backup kiln I can book for a few firings before late October, in case mine fails again.
A cafe in Roma wants 60 mugs for its opening on 14 November. I have to give them a decision by mid-October and I don't want to promise anything yet.
I'd like regular customers beyond my weekend markets, such as cafes, restaurants and small shops that would reorder.
I'm practising English twice a week and would like conversation practice, especially for dealing with clients and suppliers.
I lost a lot of work this month and I'm tired. I could use someone who understands what it's like to open a kiln and find everything ruined.
Money is tight right now and kiln repairs are using up my cushion. A new kiln is out of the question this year.
My partner is moving to Madrid for two years and I'm unsure what that means for my studio and my career. I'm curious whether I could keep making and selling in Spain.

offers.text: I hand-paint talavera-inspired plates, bowls and mugs using tin glaze, cobalt blue and a yucca brush, after two years of training in a family workshop in Puebla.
I make custom sets and can recreate a family pattern from a photo of a broken plate.
I work only with lead-free glazes, so my tableware is safe for food.
I can make small batches of matching tableware for cafes, restaurants and shops, with a fixed palette and a delivery date.
I run a stall at the Sunday market in Parque México once a month and sell through a few shops in Roma and Condesa. I have about 1,200 Instagram followers and a mailing list of 300.
I can teach a short hands-on workshop on talavera brush painting and blue-on-white glaze work for small groups.
I have a notebook of pyrometer readings from empty-kiln tests, including overshoot at the top and undershoot on cooling. I can share it with anyone diagnosing a similar fault.
I can throw on the wheel and fire in my own 80-litre electric kiln in a shared workshop in Coyoacán.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I repair electric ceramic kilns in Mexico City. A digital controller that overshoots and then undershoots often means a sticking relay or a drifting thermocouple. Could I look at your temperature logs?
catchers.can: Lucía can share her pyrometer logs and the history of what she has already replaced (thermocouple, relay), and test a hypothesis in her 11 October firing.
catchers.confirm: Do you have hands-on experience with electric kilns, meaning controllers, relays and elements, rather than only gas kilns?

catchers.hypo: I have a kiln with free slots in the next two weeks and can't use all of it. Does anyone need to fire a few shelves of earthenware?
catchers.can: Lucía could fire part of her 28 unfired dinner sets there as insurance before 28 October, and pay for the shelf space.
catchers.confirm: Can your kiln fire glazed earthenware at about 1,000 °C, and is it free before 25 October?

catchers.hypo: We're opening a restaurant in Condesa and want handmade blue-and-white plates, about 30 of them, with a consistent look.
catchers.can: Lucía can quote a matching hand-painted set, with delivery after the Day of the Dead market.
catchers.confirm: Is your delivery date in November or later, so after the Day of the Dead market?

catchers.hypo: My grandmother's hand-painted plate broke. I have photos of the pieces. Could someone make a plate with the same pattern so we can use it at family meals again?
catchers.can: Lucía can paint a new plate or a small set from the photo. She is already doing this for another client.
catchers.confirm: Is the original hand-painted earthenware, rather than porcelain or a mass-produced transfer-printed plate?

catchers.hypo: Our group of friends wants a half-day workshop to paint our own ceramic plates. We're about eight people in Mexico City.
catchers.can: Lucía can run a small brush-painting session at her workshop, after the late-October market rush.
catchers.confirm: Is your group between 4 and 10 people, in Mexico City, and flexible about a date after the first week of November?

catchers.hypo: I'm an interior designer in Madrid working on a small restaurant. I'm looking for handmade Mexican tableware, lead-free and food-safe, in small runs.
catchers.can: Lucía can send samples. A close contact who works in architecture in Madrid could also help her meet local designers and venues.
catchers.confirm: Is your project in Madrid or elsewhere in Spain, and does it need handmade, food-safe tableware in runs of under 100 pieces?

catchers.hypo: I'm a self-employed craftsperson in Mexico and I don't know how small-business accounts or an equipment loan work for someone like me.
catchers.can: Lucía can pass the question to a relative who works in a bank and can point to the right type of product. Lucía can also say how she handles it herself.
catchers.confirm: Are you self-employed and running a small craft business in Mexico, rather than a registered company with employees?

catchers.hypo: I'm a maker too, and I just lost a whole batch to a bad firing. I don't want advice, I just want to talk to someone who has been there.
catchers.can: Lucía can listen and share her own experience of opening a ruined kiln. She can't offer professional counselling.
catchers.confirm: Are you looking for peer support from another maker, not professional mental-health care?

forbids.text: I only use lead-free glazes on tableware.
I won't rush or skip steps in firings before the Day of the Dead market.
I can't commit to the Roma cafe's 60 mugs, or to any new volume order, until my kiln is proven reliable.
I can't buy a new kiln this year.
I can't take any new work with a delivery date before 28 October.
I'm unavailable on Tuesday and Thursday evenings (English class) and on the 28th, when the market stall opens at 7 am.

projects.name: Autumn tableware collection
projects.text: A collection of 40 hand-painted dinner sets for the Day of the Dead market on 28 October. Twelve are finished and the rest are waiting to be fired.

projects.name: Mugs for a Roma cafe opening
projects.text: About 60 mugs for a cafe opening on 14 November. I need to decide by mid-October, once the kiln is proven reliable.

policy.t1: When there's a real lead, I'll share details of my kiln fault and test data, my firing and market deadlines, the cafe mug order, and my production capacity.
policy.t2: Once the person and the collaboration are clear, I'll share in general terms my financial constraints, my thoughts on possibly working from Madrid, and who among my relatives could help.
policy.never: I never share my exact savings or amounts, my family's conflicts and private conversations, or details of my relationships.
